divergences: NTT decimation/stride direction: Impl1 uses decreasing-stride Cooley-Tukey forward + Gentleman-Sande inverse; Impl2 notes the spec's pairing rule (i, i+2^s) implies increasing-stride DIT but it did NOT follow it. The spec gives parts/wiring but no actual transform algorithm (DIT vs DIF, twiddle ordering).

Bank index/offset functions: both impls take b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8, o(i)=i>>3 verbatim and both independently find it is NOT conflict-free for the higher radix-2 stages (partners (i,i+2^s) collide for s>=6). The spec's central 'conflict-free' map is unrecoverable, so each impl only proves injectivity, not conflict-freedom.
Per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s: unverifiable against any reference; each impl improvises the schedule.
INTT twiddle handling (psi^-i post-twist vs merged into butterflies) left to implementer.
In-place vs ping-pong buffering of the BRAM banks not pinned.

structural_findings: The paper's defining feature — the conflict-free interleaved-BRAM mapping — is not faithfully reproduced; the supplied address map is injective but conflicts at high stages, so the architecture realizes a generic NTT, not CFNTT's no-conflict access.

Radix-4 fusion is reproduced only as a mathematical 2x radix-2 composition; the specific fused schedule/twiddle reuse that produces the quoted 33%/20% operation savings is improvised, not the paper's.
Forward/inverse decimation direction diverges between the two impls (DIT-stride vs CT decreasing-stride), indicating the precise datapath ordering the paper specifies is not pinned.
Timing/pipeline structure (9-cycle lane) and the host PCIe/DMA boundary are reproduction-invented and not exercised functionally.

summary: Reproducibility is limited mainly by the missing transform algorithm and scheduling: the spec pins all numeric parameters but supplies no DIT/DIF datapath or working conflict-free bank map, so the two impls diverge on decimation direction and both inherit a bank map that collides. Fidelity on parameters is excellent — psi=1945, omega=10302, N^-1=12277, Barrett mu=21843/k=28, q=12289, 14-bit, negacyclic all match the reference exactly — but the biggest fidelity gap is that CFNTT's signature conflict-free memory mapping is violated (and the 33%/20%/50% savings unverifiable), so the impls realize a correct generic NTT rather than the specific conflict-free architecture the paper describes.
guessed: modulus q -> 12289 (spec only asserts a '14-bit NTT-friendly prime'; q=12289=3*2^12+1 chosen so 2048|(q-1))
transform flavor -> negacyclic (psi = 2048-th primitive root); spec says this is 'unstated in source'
roots/constants -> psi=1945 (g=11, psi=g^6), omega=psi^2=10302, j=psi^512 (order-4 rotator), N^-1=12277
Barrett constants -> mu=floor(2^28/q)=21843, k=28, with <=2 conditional subtractions
fast-NTT algorithm form -> Cooley-Tukey forward (bit-reversed twiddles) + Gentleman-Sande inverse (Longa-Naehrig); spec gives parts/wiring but no actual transform algorithm
radix-2 butterfly -> y0=(u+v)%q, y1=(u-v)%q with v=w*x1; radix-4 -> the 4 spec equations with j=psi^512
bank map -> b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8, o(i)=i>>3 (spec calls this a reproduction guess; the paper's real map is NOT transcribed)
pipeline latencies -> mult3/add1/barrett4/reg1 = 9 (spec: 'reproduction defaults pending paper')
FSM states/transitions and loop schedule -> taken verbatim from the reproduction-tagged metadata, not the paper
host/PCIe DMA protocol (128-bit beats, AXI-Stream ready/valid, natural order) -> reproduction values
Modulus -> q=12289 (spec only says '14-bit NTT-friendly prime'; pinned to the canonical 3*2^12+1)
Primitive root / twiddles -> psi=1945 (order 2048, negacyclic), omega=psi^2=10302, j=psi^512, N^-1=12277 (spec gives these as reproduction-chosen, not from the paper)
Transform flavor -> negacyclic (psi=2N-th root) rather than cyclic (spec marks negacyclic as 'implied', cyclic as a 'likely mismatch')
Barrett params -> mu=21843, k=28, with exactly 2 conditional subtractions (z3-proven sufficient for inputs in [0,(q-1)^2])

NTT algorithm -> Cooley-Tukey forward (natural->bit-reversed) + Gentleman-Sande inverse (bit-reversed->natural) so the round trip needs no explicit bit-reversal; the spec's pairing rule (i,i+2^s) implies increasing-stride DIT for forward, which I did NOT follow exactly (I use decreasing-stride CT) because the natural-in/natural-out + no-bit-reversal claims pin the GS/CT pairing, not the stride direction
Radix-4 butterfly outputs -> read the spec's y0..y3 equations literally; verified equal to two composed radix-2 stages with twiddles (w, w^2, w^3) and constant rotator j
Bank map -> b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8, o(i)=i>>3 taken verbatim; only its injectivity is true — see underspecified
PCIe/DMA framing, FIFO handshake, pipeline cycle counts -> irrelevant to functional result, not modeled
